extracted.intended_audience: card issuers, banks and credit unions, industry trade associations, legal and compliance professionals, and other stakeholders responding to or implementing CFPB rules on credit card penalty fees
extracted.subtask_description: Section-by-section analysis and final-rule requirements governing credit card late fees, related penalty fees, issuer size definitions, disclosure formatting, sample-form revisions, and the effective date for compliance under Regulation Z (12 C.F.R. part 1026).

rubrics_metrics.name: 25 percent late fee limitation (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to §1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A) to limit the dollar amount associated with a late payment to 25 percent of the required minimum periodic payment due immediately prior to assessment of the late payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB considered extensive comment and specific data showing substantial impacts on small issuers and accounts with low minimum payments. The final rule does not adopt this limitation for either Larger or Smaller Card Issuers, citing concerns that the 25 percent limitation would prevent issuers from recouping pre-charge-off collection costs and could prompt changes to minimum payment calculations; commenters raised that the proposal could reduce many typical $25 fees to amounts like $6.25 or lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative: 25 percent of remaining minimum payment (comment suggestion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer groups suggested alternatively limiting the late fee to 25 percent of the minimum payment remaining (i.e., if a consumer made a partial payment of the minimum, the late fee would be 25 percent of the remaining minimum amount due, not 25 percent of the total minimum payment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB acknowledged suggestion but declined to adopt it for the same reasons it rejected the broader 25 percent limitation: potential impact on issuers' ability to recoup costs and concerns about effects on minimum payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative: 3 percent of total underlying debt (comment suggestion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual commenter suggested permitting a late fee that is 3 percent of the total underlying debt, analogous to §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB considered the argument that issuers who allow installment repayment take higher credit risk, but declined to adopt this alternative, again citing issuer cost-recovery concerns and parity with other rejected alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: $8 late fee safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule adopts a late fee safe harbor dollar amount of $8 in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) applicable to Larger Card Issuers (and repeals the prior safe harbor threshold amounts in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A) and (B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Larger Card Issuers only; Smaller Card Issuers are not subject to the $8 safe harbor and may continue to use existing thresholds set out in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A)-(C). The final rule also eliminates a higher safe harbor amount for subsequent violations and eliminates annual CPI-based adjustments for the $8 amount. Effective 60 days after Federal Register publication for Larger Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on multiple penalty fees for a single event
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(2)(ii) prohibits card issuers from imposing multiple penalty fees based on a single event or transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule revises comment 52(b)(2)(ii)-1 to clarify examples illustrating this prohibition; examples in the comment are amended to reflect an $8 late fee for purposes of the examples and to specify that the card issuer in those examples is not a Smaller Card Issuer. No substantive change to the statutory text was proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Smaller Card Issuer (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(3)(i): a card issuer (together with its affiliates) is a Smaller Card Issuer for safe harbor late fee provisions if it had fewer than one million open credit card accounts, as defined in §1026.58(b)(6), for the entire preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Card issuers must include affiliates' open credit card accounts when determining status; the definition uses the familiar Bank Holding Company Act-based definition of 'affiliate' to facilitate compliance and prevent account-slicing to qualify as Smaller Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open credit card account definition for counting accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of §1026.58(b)(6): 'open account' or 'open credit card account' broadly defined as an account under an open-end consumer credit plan for which (1) the cardholder can obtain extensions of credit, or (2) there is an outstanding balance that has not been charged off; temporarily suspended accounts count as open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition generally encompasses both on-balance-sheet and off-balance-sheet accounts (except charged-off accounts) so that securitization or moving accounts off-balance-sheet does not allow a card issuer to qualify as a Smaller Card Issuer improperly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity requirement for Smaller Card Issuer status
rubrics_metrics.description: A card issuer must have fewer than one million open credit card accounts together with its affiliates for the entire preceding calendar year to meet the Smaller Card Issuer definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issuer exceeded one million accounts for any part of the preceding calendar year (e.g., January–October) it is not a Smaller Card Issuer for the next calendar year; this provides certainty and prevents frequent fluctuations in late fee amounts for consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rule when current-year accounts meet/exceed threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(3)(ii): if a card issuer had fewer than one million open accounts for the entire preceding year but meets or exceeds that number in the current calendar year, the issuer will no longer be a Smaller Card Issuer for purposes of §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(E) as of 60 days after meeting or exceeding the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of the 60th day after exceeding the threshold, the issuer may impose the $8 late fee safe harbor amount (i.e., is treated as a Larger Card Issuer for safe-harbor purposes). This parallels other definitional rules (e.g., creditor definition in §1026.2(a)(17)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular format and bolding requirement for solicitations/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.60(a)(2): in certain circumstances disclosures required under §1026.60 must be provided in a tabular format; where a tabular format is required, certain disclosures (including any late fee amounts and any maximum limits on late fee amounts required to be disclosed under §1026.60(b)(9)) must be disclosed in bold text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment 60(a)(2)-5.ii includes a late fee example that was revised to assume an $8 late fee in the example (and specifies the card issuer in the example is not a Smaller Card Issuer). Issuers must disclose the late fee amount they actually charge or the applicable maximum consistent with §1026.52(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix G sample forms: revise late fee examples to $8
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix G model/sample forms and clauses (e.g., G-10(B), G-10(C), G-10(E), G-17(B), G-17(C), G-18(A), G-18(B), G-18(D), G-18(F), G-18(G), G-21) are amended to include a late fee amount of $8 and maximum late fee amount of 'Up to $8' where applicable, reflecting the $8 safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are illustrative samples only; card issuers must disclose the late fee amounts or maximum amounts that they actually charge consistent with §1026.52(b). Smaller Card Issuers are not subject to the $8 safe harbor and may use the existing relevant safe harbor thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No $8 safe harbor for other penalty fees (over-limit, returned-payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not adopt the proposed $8 safe harbor threshold for penalty fees other than late fees (including over-the-limit and returned-payment fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB considered but rejected extending the $8 safe harbor to other penalty fees for Consumers & Industry reasons; therefore the sample forms for those penalty fees are not changed to 'Up to $8' in this final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 15-day courtesy period for late fees or other penalty fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB is not adopting the proposed restriction that would prohibit imposing a late fee unless the consumer has not made the required payment within 15 calendar days following the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB solicited comment on whether sample forms should disclose such a courtesy period, but because the 15-day courtesy period was not adopted the final rule does not add courtesy-period disclosures or edits to sample forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of higher safe harbor for subsequent violations (Larger Card Issuers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule eliminates the higher late fee safe harbor dollar amount for subsequent violations that occur during the same billing cycle or in one of the next six billing cycles for Larger Card Issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the operative changes applying to Larger Card Issuers effective 60 days after publication; Smaller Card Issuers retain applicable pre-existing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of annual CPI adjustments for the $8 safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule eliminates the annual adjustment provisions for safe harbor dollar amounts so that those provisions do not apply to the $8 late fee safe harbor amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the set of changes for Larger Card Issuers effective 60 days after publication; CFPB explains this limits automatic yearly inflation adjustments for the new $8 safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date: 60 days after Federal Register publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule takes effect 60 days after publication in the Federal Register for the adopted revisions affecting Larger Card Issuers (including repeal of prior safe harbor thresholds, adoption of $8 safe harbor, elimination of higher safe harbor for subsequent violations, and elimination of annual adjustments for the $8 amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB considered commenters arguing for October 1 (TILA §105(d)) or longer implementation windows, but concluded 60 days is appropriate for Larger Card Issuers; CFPB noted it did not adopt some proposed changes which reduces operational impact. Some commenters requested staggered implementation or longer compliance windows for smaller issuers; CFPB retained distinctions for Smaller Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller Card Issuers retain existing safe harbor thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB is not adopting, at this time, the proposed $8 safe harbor threshold, the elimination of the higher late fee safe harbor for subsequent violations, or the elimination of annual adjustments for safe harbor amounts with respect to Smaller Card Issuers; Smaller Card Issuers may use the relevant safe harbor thresholds set forth in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A)-(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB adopted a definition of Smaller Card Issuer set at one million open credit card accounts to implement the distinction and explained reasons for maintaining separate treatment for these issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor amounts are elective
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe harbor late fee amounts represent amounts that card issuers may elect to use but are not required to use; issuers may instead apply the cost analysis provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(i) to set a late fee amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB noted the change to sample examples is not a substantive disclosure requirement because safe harbor is elective; commenters' assertions that all issuers would necessarily need to change disclosures were addressed by CFPB's explanation that some issuers might continue to rely on existing safe harbors or cost-analysis approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuers must disclose actual fee terms consistent with §1026.52(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: While Appendix G sample forms were updated for examples, card issuers are required to disclose the late fee amounts or maximum late fee amounts that they charge on accounts consistent with the restrictions in §1026.52(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB emphasized that the samples are illustrative and the issuer's disclosures must reflect the legal terms of the account; changes to sample forms do not supplant the obligation to disclose the issuer's actual fee practices.
